Consider the comparison morphism
<MATH_0001>.
Let <MATH_0002> denote the class of finite morphisms of schemes.
For <MATH_0003> in <MATH_0004> denote
<MATH_0005>
the full subcategory consisting of sheaves of the form
<MATH_0006> with <MATH_0007> in <MATH_0008>.
Then Cohomology on Sites, Properties
(<REF_0001>),
(<REF_0002>),
(<REF_0003>),
(<REF_0004>), and
(<REF_0005>)
of Cohomology on Sites, Situation
<REF_0006> hold.

We first show that <MATH_0001>
is a weak Serre subcategory by checking conditions (1), (2), (3), and (4)
of Homology, Lemma <REF_0001>.
Parts (1), (2), (3) are immediate as <MATH_0002> is exact and
fully faithful for example by Lemma <REF_0002>. If
<MATH_0003>
is a short exact sequence in <MATH_0004>
then <MATH_0005>
is exact by Lemma <REF_0003>.
Hence <MATH_0006> is in
<MATH_0007> which checks the final condition.

<STRUCT_0001><STRUCT_0002>
Cohomology on Sites, Property (<REF_0004>) holds
by the existence of fibre products of schemes
and the fact that the base change of a finite morphism of
schemes is a finite morphism of schemes, see
Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0005>.

<STRUCT_0003><STRUCT_0004>
Cohomology on Sites, Property (<REF_0006>)
follows from the commutative diagram (3) in
Topologies, Lemma <REF_0007>.

<STRUCT_0005><STRUCT_0006>
Cohomology on Sites, Property (<REF_0008>) is
Lemma <REF_0009>.

<STRUCT_0007><STRUCT_0008>
Cohomology on Sites, Property (<REF_0010>) holds by
Lemma <REF_0011> part (4).

<STRUCT_0009><STRUCT_0010>
Cohomology on Sites, Property (<REF_0012>)
is implied by
More on Morphisms, Lemma
<REF_0013>.
